pairs.why: B's paper has crisp, thick white rim edges like the real map's white border and clean flat outer contours, whereas A's wavy crumpled edges are soft and irregular with many internal fold lines.

B has cleaner, crisper silhouette edges with a clear panel structure and fewer fine grain lines, while A's dark body has many small rivets and thin pipe lines that add edge density beyond the real cards.
Both rovers have near-identical edge treatment, with the same clean contours, no outlines and similar panel seams and rivets.
A has bold, thick glass edges and a soft sculpted ice and straw silhouette like the real glass, while B's thin, fine edges (thin rim, tiny umbrella spokes) are crisper and finer than the real cards.
A's umbrella has soft scalloped panel edges and a thin pole with few internal lines, close to the real cards, while B adds thin rib struts and hub hardware that increase edge density.
A has soft, broad keycap edges with moderate seams and a thick rounded body edge like the real calculator, while B has more small, high-contrast edges in its dark keys.
A's slide has thick, soft rounded edges and few edges inside, like the real slide, while B has thin rails, thin braces and a fine tile grid that give dense, hairline edges.
A has a thick, soft rim with a clean inner bevel and a bold soft shadow edge, while B's thin glossy highlight rim and fine dot ticks add more small edges.
